item.raw_source:
import Mathlib

/--
Let $S$ be a set of rational numbers such that whenever $a$ and $b$ are members of $S$, so are $a+b$ and $ab$, and having the property that for every rational number $r$ exactly one of the following three statements is true: \[ r \in S, -r \in S, r = 0. \] Prove that $S$ is the set of all positive rational numbers.
-/
theorem putnam_1962_a6
(S : Set ℚ)
(hSadd : ∀ a ∈ S, ∀ b ∈ S, a + b ∈ S)
(hScond : ∀ r : ℚ, (r ∈ S ∨ -r ∈ S ∨ r = 0) ∧ ¬(r ∈ S ∧ -r ∈ S) ∧ ¬(r ∈ S ∧ r = 0) ∧ ¬(-r ∈ S ∧ r = 0))
: S = { r : ℚ | r > 0 } :=
sorry

by
  let S : Set ℚ := {r | r < 0}
  refine ⟨S, ?_⟩
  intro h
  have hadd : ∀ a ∈ S, ∀ b ∈ S, a + b ∈ S := by
    intro a ha b hb
    change a < 0 at ha
    change b < 0 at hb
    change a + b < 0
    linarith
  have hsign : ∀ r : ℚ, (r ∈ S ∨ -r ∈ S ∨ r = 0) ∧ ¬(r ∈ S ∧ -r ∈ S) ∧ ¬(r ∈ S ∧ r = 0) ∧ ¬(-r ∈ S ∧ r = 0) := by
    intro r
    constructor
    · rcases lt_trichotomy r 0 with hr | hr | hr
      · exact Or.inl hr
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inr hr)
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inl (by change -r < 0; linarith))
    · constructor
      · rintro ⟨hr, hnr⟩
        change r < 0 at hr
        change -r < 0 at hnr
        linarith
      · constructor
        · rintro ⟨hr, heq⟩
          change r < 0 at hr
          linarith
        · rintro ⟨hnr, heq⟩
          change -r < 0 at hnr
          linarith
  have hm := (h.mp ⟨hadd, hsign⟩).1 (-1) (by norm_num) (-1) (by norm_num)
  norm_num at hm
